story: Under a leaning Stepladder, two Railway Tracks run in beneath its frame, and where they end a Sealed Clam-Locket sits waiting — everyone gathers around it for the secret MEETING.
reading_story: Kai the surfer ducks under the Stepladder, clips his short 'kai', and joins the private MEETING.
issues: Shares Pup-Tent Roof + reading actor Kai with neighbor 界 (world); the under-roof scene (tracks + clam-locket) keeps them separable.

story: You stab a finger straight at your own nose and glare down its bridge into a mirror — the single unmistakable gesture that means ONESELF, no one else in the frame.
reading_story: Jee the clipped emcee points at his own nose, barks a sharp 'jee', and claims the mic for ONESELF.
issues: Single-component pictograph; nose-point gesture is the genuine origin, so no false etymology. Highly distinct.

story: COMPANY: on the left a smoking Roadside Shrine, and pressed against its right a fresh Mound of Soil with its sprout-marker — a brand-new firm consecrated on holy ground.
reading_story: Shaq bows at the Roadside Shrine, grunts a short 'sha', and signs the founding papers of the COMPANY.
issues: Reading actor Shaq is shared with 者 (someone); the shrine-and-soil scene is visually far from 者's mask-and-sun, so interference is low.

story: On the summit, Splayed Snowshoes stamp two outward tracks in the powder; below them, the trailhead marker of your ORIGIN sinks away as you push off, downhill, into DEPARTURE.
reading_story: Teri Hatcher tosses her sunhat off the departing ferry's rail, waving as the gangway lifts and the whistle screams DEPARTURE.
issues: Minor abstraction: 'trailhead marker of your ORIGIN sinks away' leans slightly conceptual to carry the 元/origin component; the marker object is concrete but 'origin' is doing conveyance work rather than being purely depicted.

Distinctiveness risk: 'departure' is a high-interference theme and the reading story's whistle-screams-DEPARTURE ending echoes the prior mnemonic's train-whistle-departure beat, so the two versions and neighboring departure/travel kanji could blur.
Both stories terminate on the same shouted keyword (DEPARTURE), which is on-rubric for meaning placement but slightly redundant across the pair.

story: A carved Greybeard Mask hangs up top, its long grey beard trailing down over a blazing round Sun below — the wise old face crowning the anonymous SOMEONE standing in the light.
reading_story: Shaq lifts the Greybeard Mask off the Sun, barks a short 'sha', and asks who SOMEONE hiding there could be.
issues: Uses component shapes as a scene, not asserting real etymology — no false-etymology violation. Shares Shaq with 社; mask+sun vs shrine+soil keeps them apart. Greybeard Mask recurs in 教/考 but keyword payoff differs.

story: GROUND: on the left a fresh Mound of Soil with its sprout-marker, and slithering into its right side a slick River Eel, burrowing its lazy S-curve down into the packed earth.
reading_story: Chee the clipped cheerleader taps the Mound of Soil, chirps a short 'chee', and stamps flat the solid GROUND.
issues: River Eel is a vivid unique actor; Chee reading actor and burrowing-into-earth scene are unambiguous.

story: On the Horizon Line stand Twin Pillars flanking a Tree; a Kings Crown is jammed onto a Woolly Ram lashed to an Ox-Plow, and a Lightning Bolt splits the whole rig — the family BUSINESS.
reading_story: Gyo drawls his name looong as he signs off on the crown-topped ram, launching the BUSINESS.
issues: Dense 7-actor scene, but the crown-on-ram anchor is memorable; reading_story correctly encodes the long ō via 'looong'.

story: A weathered wooden signpost, arm swinging in the wind at the crossroads, points its single crooked finger down the lonely road — that way, the only DIRECTION out of town.
issues: Monolithic learned kanji; single-actor scene, vivid signpost image ties directly to DIRECTION. Kun-dominant, so no reading actor — correct.

story: On a Mound of Soil to the left, someone plants a tattered Skull-and-Crossbones Flag while the blazing Sun hangs above it — a marked-off, guarded LOCATION nobody may cross.
issues: All three actors named; clear left-to-right spatial layout. Kun-dominant, no reading actor — correct.

story: A proud diver on a springboard plants both feet wide, chest thrown out, arms flung high — the instant before the leap, holding perfectly still, refusing to sit: STAND UP.
issues: Monolithic learned kanji; the diver's planted stance is a strong pictographic match to the glyph shape and to STAND UP. Kun-dominant, no reading actor — correct.

story: On the left, a sapling forces itself to STAND UP straight atop the Tree's stump; on the right, Woodsman Hatchet swings down and splits the old bark away, exposing pale, NEW wood beneath.
reading_story: Shinn, the night bartender, slides a crisp bill across the bar and grins — his first NEW customer of the season, tip still warm.
issues: Minor: the keyword 'NEW' is not the final word of the meaning story ('exposing pale, NEW wood beneath') — it sits at the end but with a two-word tail; acceptable for 'end' placement but a tighter ending would land NEW last.
Minor: 'sapling' reads as new-growth framing rather than a named persona, so it is not a phantom component, but it slightly overlaps the Tree's role and could be conflated with it.

story: The two heavy doors of a Castle Gate swing wide, and inside the gap two Cupped Palms lift a Horizon Line like a bar off its brackets — throwing the whole gate OPEN.
issues: All three actors named; the palms-lifting-the-bar image is an excellent semantic fit to OPEN. Kun-dominant, no reading actor — correct.

story: A single splayed HAND presses flat against the glass, all five fingers spread wide and the thumb hooked off to one side, the palm mashed white — nothing on the pane but one bare HAND.
A single Flexing Bicep bulges hard on the empty table, veins popping along the strained muscle with no body attached, curling an invisible weight — nothing here but pure raw POWER.
A straw Scarecrow tears itself off its post and jams a slanted Ritual Stake into the empty socket to stand guard in its place while it slips away — the perfect SUBSTITUTE.
reading_story: Dyer swaps in a Ritual Stake, snaps a clipped 'dai,' and lets it SUBSTITUTE for the departed Scarecrow.

story: The blazing Sun on the left and the silver Full Moon on the right hang side by side in one sky, pouring their combined glow down over the whole valley — dazzlingly BRIGHT.
issues: Sun+Moon is a common textbook mnemonic for 明; low interference risk but shares imagery with other Sun/Moon glyphs.

story: On the left a heavy grand piano sits frozen to the ice; from the right the Flexing Bicep slams into it, sending it screeching across the lake — MOVE.
reading_story: In the morgue, the corpse tagged 'Doe' sits bolt upright, moans a long 'dōōō', and starts to MOVE.

story: A huge unblinking Watching Eye fills the whole doorway, a tall dark pupil pinned dead center, tracking you across the room without a single flicker — one enormous staring EYE.
A fat comic Speech Bubble floats up from the debater's mouth, stacked lines of words crammed inside behind its little lid — everything he could ever SAY, crystallized in one balloon.
issues: Single-component glyph; the Speech Bubble already carries the SAY meaning natively, so the story is more decorative than load-bearing — still vivid and passes cleanly.

story: LOGIC: the King's Crown is balanced dead-center on top of a weathered Village Milestone, and only by reasoning out each carved marking on the stone can you deduce which road leads home.
reading_story: Lee bows to the King's Crown atop the Village Milestone, then argues its route with flawless LOGIC.
issues: Both Kings Crown (王) and Village Milestone (里) appear in story and reading_story; Lee matches the り on'yomi persona. 'King's Crown' with apostrophe is cosmetically off from registry 'Kings Crown' but is the same actor. LOGIC lands hard at the very start.

story: On the left, the Scarecrow drags an anatomy book to its right side, tears out the pages, and stuffs them under its straw — organ by organ building itself a real BODY.
reading_story: Ty Cobb slides spikes-first into home plate, slamming his whole BODY into the catcher.

story: Seen from above, a flooded Rice-Paddy Grid stretches out, mud dikes carving it into a neat four-square window of shining water — one perfect RICE FIELD.
issues: Single-component pictograph; Rice-Paddy Grid actor is itself the meaning, so the story mostly restates the image — but the four-square-window framing is highly imageable and the RICE FIELD keyword lands cleanly at end.

story: One glossy Ink Droplet hovers directly above the King's Crown, and the instant it falls to anoint the jewels, the crowned figure beneath is proclaimed LORD of the whole realm.
reading_story: Shu tips the Ink Droplet onto the King's Crown, anointing himself LORD with a single clipped nod.
issues: Ink Droplet (丶) placed above Kings Crown (王) — spatially faithful. Shu matches the しゅ on'yomi persona. 'King's Crown' apostrophe cosmetically diverges from registry 'Kings Crown', same actor. LORD lands at end of both stories.

story: A Judge's Gavel bangs down hard on the spine of a Cracked Conch propped upright like a page — cracking it open to reveal, glowing on its pale surface, the day's TOPIC.
reading_story: Amanda Dyer dips a fresh page into indigo, and the single word she dyes across it, dripping blue, is the class TOPIC.
issues: Minor: the main story leans on 'propped upright like a page' and the reading story reuses 'page' — the page motif is drawn from the Cracked Conch's own image ("held up like a printed page"), so it is not a phantom component, but reviewers should confirm 'page' is never mistaken for a separate actor.

Minor: the keyword payoff 'the day's TOPIC' glowing on a surface is slightly abstract; it is rendered imageably (a glowing inscription) so it lands, but 'topic' remains the least concrete element in an otherwise vivid scene.

story: A Falling Katana slashes down, skids flat along the Horizon Line, flicks off one black Ink Droplet, and a Lightning Bolt cracks straight through it all — every answer it offers comes back NEGATIVE.
reading_story: A Foo Fighter, clipped and short — 'foo!' — shakes his head at every request, purely NEGATIVE.

story: MAKE: a straw Scarecrow at the left edge grips a Falling Katana slashing down, and where its silver edge meets a Lightning Bolt cracking straight down, sparks weld two beams together into something new.
issues: Payoff 'weld two beams into something new' is slightly abstract; the concrete welding action mostly carries it.

story: You grab the well-worn UTILIZE tool off its hook, its handle polished smooth by a thousand jobs — the one gadget you reach for and put to use every single time.
reading_story: Yo-Yo Ma draws his long bow across the cello — yooo — and UTILIZEs every string to fill the hall.
issues: Single whole-kanji component leaves the story with no structural hooks; generic 'well-worn tool' imagery risks interfering with other tool-based scenes. Reading_story with Yo-Yo Ma's long bow is the more memorable anchor.

story: A stubby Wall Peg juts out up top; slung on it hangs a heavy UTILIZE toolbox. Both crash down onto a rubber Conveyor Belt scrolling along the bottom-left — funneling everything into roaring TRAFFIC.
reading_story: A colossal Tsunami rips a Conveyor Belt from the street and hurls cars sideways, drowning the gridlocked TRAFFIC under its towering wall of water.
issues: Main story is ~42 words, marginally over the ~40-word target (within tolerance but on the edge).

Spatial fidelity is loose for 用/UTILIZE: it has no stated position and the peg+toolbox 'crash down onto' the belt, whereas 用 is actually the main body with 辶 wrapping the bottom-left. Broadly faithful but the causal chain (peg -> toolbox -> belt -> traffic) is busy.
In the reading_story, 'TRAFFIC' is the payoff but is trailed by 'under its towering wall of water', slightly softening the end placement (still acceptable).

story: Under a slanted Cliff Awning, a flat Horizon Line rests above a yawning Trap Pit, and a yellow Rubber Glove reaches in to twist a dial notch by notch — measuring the exact DEGREES.
reading_story: Homer, groaning 'DOH!', reads the thermometer's DEGREES climbing far too high.
issues: The 'dial'/'notch' prop is added scaffolding to land the keyword, not a component — acceptable as it stays a mnemonic device and makes no etymological claim; the four actors are all faithfully placed.

story: STRONG: a taut yew Longbow bends into a fierce arc, a Sealed Clam-Locket clenched in its grip, and a plump Fat Grub coils along the string — flexing so hard even the worm bulges with muscle.
A turkey Wishbone snaps apart at the top, and beneath the split a Sealed Clam-Locket springs wide open, spilling its private secret onto the town square for everyone to read — now it's PUBLIC.
reading_story: Coe, drawing his name out looong, reads the opened locket aloud until the whole PUBLIC square has heard it.

story: At the arcade's left edge, the Grabber Claw plunges, hooks the swing-log of a colossal Bronze Temple Bell, and hauls the whole ringing bell up against the glass — refusing to release, it will HOLD that prize forever.
reading_story: Emcee Jee, clipped as ever, barks "HOLD!" — and the crowd freezes mid-cheer, every arm locked in place, gripping their pose until Jee finally snaps his fingers.

story: A tall Long Halberd stands planted beside a Village Milestone, a rusty Meat Hook dangling off its shaft — the last markers before the road dissolves into endless open PLAINS.
reading_story: Yah, clipped and sharp, plants the Long Halberd at the milestone and yells one short 'ya!' across the empty PLAINS.

story: BY MEANS OF a wobbly Stepladder, an Ink Droplet climbs to the ceiling while a Lightning Bolt crackles up the rungs beside it — the ladder alone lets both reach the top.
reading_story: Eaton, clipped to a sharp 'ee,' scales the Stepladder and paints the ceiling BY MEANS OF one dripping Ink Droplet.
issues: Reading_story reworded 'brush' to 'Ink Droplet' so the dripping actor is named explicitly, avoiding an unregistered 'brush' prop.

story: A steep Thatched House caps the scene, its eaves sloping wide, and snug beneath its roof a bristly Muddy Boar snorts and roots in the warm straw — every creature's cozy HOUSE.
A flat Horizon Line stretches across the era, and a Lightning Bolt cracks straight down through it, splitting the timeline in two — one bolt ending an old GENERATION and starting the next.
reading_story: Seth, clipped and quick, plants his flag on the Horizon Line and claims this whole GENERATION as his own.
issues: The '世' component is the whole-glyph self-reference (no image/actor); it is carried by the keyword GENERATION itself rather than a distinct actor, which is correct for this degenerate component. Only the two visual components (Horizon Line, Lightning Bolt) are dramatized.

story: Inside a snug Thatched House an elegant Hourglass tips over on the hearth, her sand whispering softly bulb to bulb while the fire pops — nothing to do but sink into the cushions and RELAX.
HEART: a fat red valentine heart thumps alone on the table, three quivering droplets of feeling flicked off its curved bottom, beating so hard the whole room pulses with each warm thud.
issues: Three droplets nicely mirror the three dots of 心; they are scene detail, not a named phantom component, so gating is clean.

story: A flooded Rice-Paddy Grid sits up top, and pinned beneath it a red valentine Heart pounds — squeeze the field-brain and the heart together and you feel your whole mind strain to THINK.
issues: Shares the Rice-Paddy Grid with 界/画 and the Heart with 心; the field-over-heart spatial arrangement keeps it distinct.

story: A leaning Stepladder caps a flooded Rice-Paddy Grid, and the whole field balances on two stubby Wishing-Well Legs that stride off past the horizon — one paddy carrying the entire WORLD.
reading_story: Kai the surfer paddles clean off the edge of the map, hooting as he drops into a whole new WORLD.
issues: Kai (short diphthong ai) matches the surfer persona; reading_story keeps the WORLD payoff at the end.

story: A Greybeard Mask leans over a Swaddle Basket up front, and behind it a Cracking Whip snaps down hard, driving the drowsy baby to sit up and finally learn — this is how elders TEACH.
reading_story: Kyo the frontman howls a loooong lesson over the basket, stretching every word until the child learns what he means to TEACH.
issues: Kyo (long ō) persona honored and the long vowel encoded via 'loooong / stretching every word'; Greybeard Mask shared with 者/考 but the whip-and-basket scene is unmistakable.

story: SENTENCE: a proud calligraphed character stands cross-legged like a little scholar, arms flung wide over a crossed sash, every printed stroke of it linking into one clean written line.
reading_story: Bunn presses his fresh bakery roll onto the page and stamps out one perfect SENTENCE in warm doughy ink.
issues: Registry gives Bunn only a phonetic note (voiced twin of Fun, ends -n); the bakery-roll image is the generator's persona and is used consistently, no contradiction. SENTENCE lands at story start and reading_story end.

story: Down two shining Railway Tracks a wishing well rolls along on its stubby Wishing-Well Legs, tracing every line all the way back to where the very first well was dug — the ORIGIN.
reading_story: Glenn kneels at the Wishing-Well Legs and drops a coin, wishing to return to the ORIGIN.
issues: The 元 (origin, already-learned) component is carried only by the abstract 'first well was dug' payoff rather than a concrete actor, but the keyword lands cleanly.

story: On the right rises the Terraced Hill; at its zigzag summit a Finish-Line Tape snaps across the entrance gate, welcoming exhausted pilgrims into the marble-columned INSTITUTION.
reading_story: Quinn, in mascara and jester cap, cuts the ribbon and marches proudly into the newly opened INSTITUTION.
issues: Minor: 'marble-columned' and 'welcoming exhausted pilgrims' add flavor not tied to any component, but they are harmless decoration, not phantom mandatory elements.

Minor: reading_story leans on the reading-actor persona note (jester cap/mascara for Harley Quinn) but does not restate the visual glyph components; this is acceptable since the reading_story only needs the reading actor plus keyword.

story: Atop a lone Village Milestone, someone stacks a THOUSAND identical milestones — a swaying tower crushing the little stone signpost flat into the paddy mud. Nothing on earth is this HEAVY.
reading_story: Juno hoists the THOUSAND-stone tower onto one shoulder, muscles bulging, grinning because to her the impossibly HEAVY load feels light as foam.
issues: Minor: in reading_story the keyword 'HEAVY' sits mid-clause ('the impossibly HEAVY load feels light as foam') rather than at start/end — acceptable since the meaning payoff lands cleanly at the end of the main story, but the reading story's keyword placement is softer than ideal.

Minor: 千 is carried as a bare concept word ('a THOUSAND') rather than an embodied actor — correct per the record (it has null actor/image, only kanji_keyword 'thousand'), but it is the less vivid of the two components.

story: A Woodsman Hatchet, still shuddering in its chopping block, glides down a rubber Conveyor Belt toward you, and you flinch as its blade whirs NEAR your nose, then NEARER.
reading_story: Martin Luther King steps NEAR the podium, so close the front row feels his breath.

story: An old sage's Greybeard Mask hangs up top, and a soft Swaddling Wrap folds down beneath it, hugging his chin as he strokes the long beard slowly — taking his time to CONSIDER.
issues: Shares the Greybeard Mask with 者/教; the Swaddling Wrap + beard-stroking 'think it over' action keeps it separable.

story: A flat Horizon Line caps the top, an open Trap Pit drops beneath it, and inside the pit a Rice-Paddy Grid is framed square — a neatly bordered PICTURE.
reading_story: Garr leans over the Trap Pit and admires the framed Rice-Paddy Grid like a museum PICTURE.

story: On the far left, Puddle Splash flicks three fat droplets into a puddle — every splash balloons into a rolling wave, wave upon wave swelling outward until the puddle becomes one endless SEA.
reading_story: Kai the surfer paddles out at dawn, snaps a clipped "Kai!" as he drops down a glassy wave — the whole SEA is his.

story: A War Helmet perches up top, a white Bedsheet Cover drapes its face below, and two Wishing-Well Legs prop the whole disguised figure at the market stall, hawking wares to every passerby — everything must SELL.
A stern Marble Bust rides upright on its plinth atop a rubber Conveyor Belt at the bottom-left, chin lifted, gliding forever down one long straight ROAD.
reading_story: A wide-eyed Doe steps onto the ROAD, hooves clicking, following the painted centre-line as it stretches endlessly toward the horizon.
issues: Minor: 'gliding forever' in the main story is mildly abstract compared to the otherwise concrete imagery; a fixed distance or landmark would sharpen it, but it does not break imageability.
Minor: main story and reading_story both lean on the 'endless/endlessly toward the horizon' road motif, creating slight redundancy between the two beats.

story: A fat Stumpy Sparrow flops down onto a bare Tree, and hundreds more grumpy old birds pile in after it, cramming every branch of the trunk — a whole flock come to GATHER.
A Speech Bubble on the left crammed with numbers reads them aloud, while on the right a Plus-Sign Crossroads adds each figure lane by lane, tallying the total exactly — the words MEASURE every count.
reading_story: Kayo the cabaret dancer stretches a long 'kayyy' as she counts each spin, MEASURING her twirls one by one.

story: PRIVATE: on the left a golden Rice Stalk bows its heavy head, and tucked at its base a Sealed Clam-Locket stays clasped shut, hoarding one secret grain no one else may ever see.
MORNING: an early bird struts beneath the freshly painted Plus-Sign Crossroads, screeching everyone awake, while to the right the pale Full Moon gives up and sinks.
reading_story: Cho zooms her broom through the MORNING sky, howling a long "Chōōō!" as she snatches breakfast toast right off your plate.

story: A Canvas-Top Jeep, engine growling, rolls onto a rubber Conveyor Belt sweeping up from the lower-left, and the belt hauls the whole jeep steadily forward down the road to CARRY.
reading_story: Unwin sprints alongside the belt, wrestling the growling jeep back on track as it fights to CARRY itself off the edge.

story: A wooden Spooled Thread on the left unwinds its last strand, which freezes solid the instant it touches the bitter WINTER frost stacked on the right — the very END.
reading_story: A cobbler hammers a Shoe onto a customer's foot, drives the final nail, and grins: the long day of work has reached its END.

story: Under the slanted roof of a Cliff Awning, a single Sealed Clam-Locket sits tucked in one corner, dwarfed by all the empty sheltered floor stretching around it — the shelter is astonishingly WIDE.
The Scarecrow stands stiff at the left edge of a muddy field; to its right the lord of the manor drags his four-poster bed into the furrows — this is where he will DWELL.
reading_story: Juno arrives with mountains of luggage and nails her nameplate to the door: this is where Juno will DWELL, forever.

story: Dead center on the Plus-Sign Crossroads sits an Open Toolbox, its tools gleaming upward. A mechanic kneels, tests each wrench, and swears every single one is genuine, honest, TRUE.
reading_story: Shinn the bartender slides a polished glass across the bar and vows the whiskey inside is the real, unwatered, TRUE stuff.

story: A Falling Katana slashes down across a flat Horizon Line, and hanging below in the dark a lone Full Moon glows — the one treasure the hoarding dragon keeps clutched to its chest, all it will POSSESS.
reading_story: Yuna glides a long looping arc under the Full Moon, hugging the trophy she alone will POSSESS.
issues: The hoarding dragon is a scene-dressing prop, not a phantom component — acceptable, but the katana/horizon/moon are the load-bearing actors.

story: A wide-open cartoon Open Mouth, square as a letterbox, screams so loud the windows rattle; you toss in an onigiri and the square lips snap shut — MOUTH.
reading_story: Coe collapses past the finish line, MOUTH gaping into a huge square, dragging in one looong slow breath as the crowd roars.

story: Under a flat Horizon Line roof, a Goalpost Frame stands wide, and inside its uprights a single Open Mouth chants — every voice in the crowd shouting the exact SAME word in unison.
A Rake Hand up top drags across a flat Horizon Line, snags a hanging Meat Hook, and hauls an Open Mouth up out of the dirt — sorting out one urgent MATTER at the office.
reading_story: Jee, the clipped emcee, barks one short 'jee!' and settles the whole MATTER on the spot.

story: Behind the shop counter, a wide Open Mouth perches atop a giant Cowrie Shell, bellowing "Welcome!" at every customer while the shell rattles with the day's coins — the perfect EMPLOYEE.
reading_story: Quinn's grinning portrait hangs above the register: "EMPLOYEE of the Month — Quinn." She curtsies with her mallet whenever a customer reads it.

story: Both doors of a Castle Gate swing wide, and framed dead center in the gap a single Open Mouth hangs, lips parted mid-word — hurling one sharp QUESTION at whoever dares approach.
reading_story: Monn leans through the Castle Gate, purses her lips, and coos a clipped 'mon?' — one flirtatious QUESTION.

story: A shiny Pot Lid caps the skyline; beneath it an Open Mouth roars a proclamation, and a fine Sand Trickle sifts down from the balcony below — the whole grand tower is the nation's CAPITAL.
reading_story: Kyo, the howling frontman, holds his name loooong from the tower balcony, screaming his anthem across the CAPITAL.

story: A Feathered Arrow streaks in dead straight from the left and thunks into an Open Mouth on the right, jamming the answer down its throat so fast that instantly, without a blink, you KNOW.
On the left an Open Mouth gasps above a straining Flexing Bicep; on the right a tall Guillotine Blade drops and cleaves the two apart, slicing head clean from muscle — SEPARATE.
reading_story: Better, gritting his teeth, gives one short clipped grunt as the blade SEPARATES the pieces — bett, and it's cut.

story: The Clipboard Clerk, on the right, signs out the stiff Scarecrow propped at his left and scrubs the office windows with its straw head — everything on his clipboard gets put to USE.
reading_story: The Sheriff pries a bottle open with his tin star — a clipped "shi!" of escaping fizz. The Sheriff will USE anything.

story: One Open Mouth gapes up top, and two more Open Mouths gape side by side beneath it — three hungry buyers all shouting orders at once for the shop's stacked GOODS.
reading_story: Benny Hinn presses a hand to each of the three mouths, sharply blessing his GOODS with one clipped hinn.
issues: Dropped '品' from components_used: the supplied second component is the target kanji itself (null image), not a distinct actor; the three-mouth structure fully renders it via Open Mouth.

story: On your marks: the elegant Hourglass presses her pinched waist against the granite pedestal on her right; the instant glass touches stone, sand roars downward — the race can BEGIN.
reading_story: The Sheriff fires one clipped shot — "Shi!" — and every duel in town must BEGIN on his signal.

story: Perched up top, a Sealed Clam-Locket clamps shut on a secret; directly below it a wide Open Mouth props open, jaw locked flat and steady — together they form the sturdy PEDESTAL holding a trophy aloft.
reading_story: Dyer taps the trophy on its PEDESTAL, gives a clipped 'dai,' and the whole stand doesn't wobble an inch.

story: A Falling Katana slashes straight down through a thin Sand Trickle, and its blade scatters all but a handful of grains into the wind — only a FEW stubborn specks cling to the edge.
Left, the Rice-Paddy Grid stretches its flooded squares; right, a giant Iron Nail is hammered upright at the edge, and pinned to that nail hangs the wooden sign marking this new TOWN.
reading_story: Cho hammers her wand like an Iron Nail into a wooden post, and the whole muddy hamlet suddenly springs up around her into a real TOWN.

story: On the left, Scattered Rice Grains spill across the counter; on the right a Grain Dipper scoops them up and levels each measure — you pay by the dipperful, and that scoop sets the FEE.
reading_story: Ryo the hardboiled detective drops a long, drawling 'ryō,' pays the Grain Dipper's FEE, and pockets the last scoop of rice.

story: A single red I-Beam Girder lies bolted flat, its riveted flanges gleaming under the welding sparks — the raw backbone of every workshop's CRAFT.
reading_story: Coe hoists the I-Beam Girder overhead, holds a long ringing 'kooo,' and welds it into place with sheer CRAFT.
issues: Trimmed the original 'bolted flat across two others' — that phrasing implied extra girders beyond the single supplied component. Welding sparks/rivets are scene dressing, not named phantom components, so kept for imageability.

story: A Writing Brush stands upright at the center, ink dripping, while a springy Vaulting Pole sweeps in from the lower-left and launches it skyward — and where the brush lands, they BUILD a tower.
A dark Burrow Hole gapes in the ceiling; below it a red I-Beam Girder, propped up by its craft, spans a vast echoing hall that holds absolutely nothing — swept EMPTY.
reading_story: Coombs presses his ear to the EMPTY airport hangar, hearing his own long "kuu" echo back across the deserted floor.
issues: Minor (non-gating): 'propped up by its craft' leans on the abstract keyword of 工 rather than a crisp physical action of the I-Beam Girder, a slight imageability soft spot. Consider a more concrete verb (e.g., the girder bracing/spanning the hall) to fully picture the component.

Note (not a defect): the meaning story teaches keyword EMPTY while the reading story teaches on'yomi くう (Coombs) rather than the dominant kun reading から — this is correct by design (reading registry is on'yomi-only, §1.3; くう drives 空気/空港), so no gate is violated.

story: HURRY: a Rake Hand claws frantically at the dirt, a Swaddling Wrap yanks a bundle tight in one snatch, and a pounding heart hammers beneath — all of it racing against the clock.
reading_story: Governor Cuomo, name stretched loooong — kyuuu — sprints in with a Rake Hand still clutched, gasping at everyone to HURRY.
issues: Long-vowel cue (kyuuu, loooong) correctly matches Cuomo's long ū.

story: A lone traffic bollard plants itself dead in the middle of the road, immovable — nothing on wheels gets past it, everything must STOP.
issues: Trimmed the 'boot-print at its base' detail: 止 is supplied as a single already-learned kanji with no sub-actor, so the added footprint risked reading as a phantom component. Bollard=STOP carries the whole load.

story: CORRECT: on a flat Horizon Line the STOP-bollard stands bolt upright, plumb and square, its edges aligned to perfection — a mark so exactly true the teacher ticks it right.
issues: Fixed grammar ('teacher tick it' -> 'teacher ticks it'). Reuses the STOP-bollard actor consistently with the 止 story.

story: Under an open SKY, the Twin Pillars hold a wrapped parcel between them; a rubber Conveyor Belt sweeps along the bottom-left and whisks the parcel away to SEND it off.
reading_story: Sosa the courier bellows "Sooo-ō, awaaay it goes!", drawing the long ō out as she leans on the pillars to SEND the last crate down the belt.

story: A broad butcher's Cleaver on the right swings down and shears a Soup Ladle clean in two on the left, its bowl clattering apart — one crisp stroke to CUT.
A wooden Cartwheel on the left spins so fast its Railway Tracks blur past, and a Sealed Clam-Locket lashed to the hub whirls round and round on the right — the whole rig REVOLVES.
reading_story: Detective Tennison clips out 'ten!' as the Cartwheel REVOLVES, tracking the spinning Sealed Clam-Locket through one full turn.

story: A grey Boulder rests on a wooden Sawhorse; a craftsman drags the stone back and forth along the crossbar until its rough flank gleams to a mirror POLISH.
reading_story: Ken the plastic doll spits on his sleeve and rubs the trophy until it shines with a blinding POLISH.
issues: Minor: the unlisted 'craftsman' agent is harmless narrative glue, not a phantom component, but ideally the action would be driven by a named component actor or the reader themselves.
Distinctiveness is only moderate — 'polish stone until it shines' risks blending with other polish/shine mnemonics; the sawhorse-crossbar-as-abrasive-surface is the main saving hook.

story: An Open Mouth gapes wide at the top, and sprouting straight down beneath the shouting square hangs a single bare limb — knee bent, foot planted flat on the floor: one whole LEG.
issues: Fixed: original buried LEG mid-sentence (failed 'meaning lands'); rewrote so LEG is the payoff at the end. Kun reading, so no reading actor (correct).

story: A Curled Cat, all nine lives folded into a comma, wriggles deep beneath the dark Burrow Hole in the bank, scratching frantic diagrams into the earthen wall of its den — obsessive RESEARCH.
reading_story: Governor Cuomo squeezes into the burrow, notepad out, cross-examining a cat about its nine lives — footage he swears is groundbreaking RESEARCH.

story: MUSIC: two Frost Beads shiver at the very top, a White Candle glows in the middle, and a bare Tree spreads its branches below — pluck each icy bead like a string and the candlelit Tree sings.
reading_story: Gackt the rock star snaps a clipped 'gaku', flicks the Frost Beads, and the whole Tree erupts into roaring MUSIC.
issues: 'clipped gaku' correctly cues Gackt's short -ku coda.

story: A Woolly Ram crowns the top; a Falling Katana slices its diagonal slash straight down its chest; at the bottom a Watching Eye peers out from the wool the ram has pulled over itself to WEAR.
reading_story: A Chuckler snatches the fleece off the rack, shrugs it on, and cannot stop laughing at how the coat he chose to WEAR swallows him whole.

story: Beneath the slanted Cliff Awning, a Fortune Booth's divining rod swings toward glittering shelves of goods, drawing shoppers into the shaded shelter to browse and buy — a thriving roadside STORE.
reading_story: Detective Tennison stakes out the midnight STORE, magnifying glass raised, catching a thief slipping goods off the shelves into his coat.
issues: Minor: the reading_story reuses 'shelves'/'goods' from the main story, so the two stories share commercial scene-dressing; acceptable but slightly reduces the reading story's independent memorability.

Minor: the 'store with shelves and shoppers' framing is somewhat generic; distinctiveness rests mainly on the cliff-awning + fortune-booth + divining-rod combination rather than the shop scene itself.

story: A Bronze Medal, still warm from the race, is pinned to the pillow of a Leaning Sickbed — the athlete who won it now shivers under the fever-cloth, too ILL to stand.
reading_story: Beau limps into the ward clutching his Bronze Medal, coughing a long "byooo" as the nurse confirms he is truly ILL.

story: A Woodsman Hatchet, then a second Woodsman Hatchet, chop clean through a fat Cowrie Shell on the block — splitting it to prove the coin is solid silver, top-grade QUALITY.
reading_story: Schitt bites the coin, then swaps it for a mouthful of QUALITY caviar, spitting the fake shell aside.
issues: Gate 4 (meaning lands): PASS but note QUALITY appears in BOTH stories — cleanly at the end of the main story (meaning_placement 'end'), and again mid-clause in the reading story ('QUALITY caviar'). The reading-story reuse is unnecessary; the payoff should live in one story to keep the cue clean.

Gate 5/12 (actor consistency & coherence): the reading story's second beat is weak — 'swaps it for a mouthful of QUALITY caviar, spitting the fake shell aside' introduces a 'fake' framing that contradicts the main story's 'prove the coin is solid silver / top-grade' and adds an unmotivated caviar prop. Coherent enough not to gate, but it lowers distinctiveness/coherence.

Distinctiveness caveat: the 'prove it's solid / top-grade quality' payoff is somewhat generic for a Substance/Quality/Matter kanji and could interfere with value/substance neighbors; the hatchet+cowrie imagery is what carries the distinctiveness.
Positive note (not a defect): the doubled 'Woodsman Hatchet, then a second Woodsman Hatchet' correctly mirrors the 斤斤 top of 質 over the 貝 base — good spatial fidelity.

story: The Forked Footpath dead-ends at the Bronze Temple Bell hanging on the right; the way opens only when it tolls, so you kneel beneath the cold bronze rim and WAIT.
reading_story: Ty crouches at the plate, bat cocked, refusing to swing — pitch after pitch, he'll WAIT for the perfect one.

story: A Speech Bubble on the left barks "Ready?" while Ceremony Scissors on the right snip wildly at empty air, snapping open and shut again and again as they TRY to cut a ribbon that isn't there.
reading_story: The Sheriff spits, "Go ahead, TRY it," daring the outlaw to draw first outside the saloon.

story: Direction stands on the left pointing the way while a Feathered Arrow streaks off to the right, and everyone following that banner and that arrow marches as one loyal TRIBE.
reading_story: Zocker, grunting a hard zoku, fires his Feathered Arrow to rally the whole TRIBE behind him.
issues: 方 is the already-learned kanji 'direction' rather than a named actor, correctly referenced by keyword; 'hard zoku' cues Zocker's voiced/short -ku coda.

story: A flat-topped Still Butte looms on the left, rooted and unmoving; beside it on the right a gleaming Gold Ingot sits, but the desert moonlight bleaches its shine cold and pale — pure SILVER.
reading_story: Ginn taps the frosted Ingot against the Still Butte, and each clipped 'gin' rings out bright as fresh SILVER.

story: EARLY at dawn, the round Sun sits low over a Plus-Sign Crossroads, its first light glinting on the empty tarmac while the whole town still sleeps and no car has yet passed.
A Falling Katana slashes down and strikes a big orange Starfish sprawled below, and the low Sun catches the water so the whole sprawled shape shimmers on the still lake surface — a perfect REFLECT.
reading_story: Abe leans over the pond, holds a long 'eeei', and watches his own drawn-out face REFLECT back at him.
issues: Shares Falling Katana + Starfish with 英 (england); the Sun component and lake/reflection framing are the distinguishing hooks.

story: A PARENT will STAND UP on a Tree stump at dawn, hoisting a Periscope high to watch their toddler wobble across the yard, one anxious round lens never blinking.
reading_story: Shinn the bartender STANDS UP on a barstool, waving to the anxious PARENT peering through the door, promising the lost kid is safe inside.

story: A Stepladder props open an Open Mouth on the left; on the right a Galloping Stallion thunders straight along the flat Horizon Line, and the examiner shouts every answer down its throat — the ultimate driving TEST.
reading_story: Ken the plastic doll grips the Stallion's reins with a clipped 'ken' and passes his riding TEST on the first try.

story: A Grass Tuft crowns the top, and beneath its green blades a Falling Katana slices down onto a big orange Starfish sprawled below — the tea-garden crest flying over ENGLAND.
reading_story: Abe raises a long 'eeei' cheer, waving the flag proudly over ENGLAND at the garden party.
issues: Shares Falling Katana + Starfish (and the Abe reading actor) with 映 (reflect); the Grass Tuft crown plus the England/crest framing are the distinguishing hooks.

story: A Feathered Arrow, snapped off in a soldier's side, lies locked inside a Toolbox Tray of splints and bandages — the field DOCTOR reaches in and eases it free.
reading_story: Eaton snaps a sharp 'ee', tweezes the Feathered Arrow out of the Toolbox Tray, and works on as the battlefield DOCTOR.

story: A stiff Scarecrow on the left snaps to attention and lifts a polished War Helmet in both arms, presenting it to its lord — dutiful and ready to SERVE.
reading_story: The Sheriff clips a sharp 'shi', sets the War Helmet on the Scarecrow, and swears to SERVE the town.

story: A Sealed Clam-Locket rests atop a fresh Mound of Soil like a grave-marker; you set it down, turn your back on the plot, and LEAVE for good.
reading_story: Cole clips a short 'kyo', lays the Sealed Clam-Locket on the Mound of Soil, and turns to LEAVE.

story: The Open Mouth on the left gapes wide as an Unripe Peach, hard and green, drops in from the right. One reckless bite — sour, puckering, electric — floods the tongue with raw FLAVOR.
reading_story: Mee bites the Unripe Peach, winces, and whispers a clipped "Mee!" — even sour, that jolt is unmistakable FLAVOR.
issues: Minor: 'sour, puckering, electric' is the least imageable stretch — puckering is picturable but 'electric' is abstract; a concrete visual (e.g. a visible zap on the tongue) would push imageability to 5.

Minor: 口 'Open Mouth' is a high-frequency component that recurs across many kanji, so the mouth alone carries little distinctiveness — the Unripe-Peach + sour-jolt pairing is what makes this card unique, and it does carry that load adequately.
Observation (not a defect): the candidate correctly drops all four phantom components from previous_mnemonic (Pot Lid, Lightning-Bolt trunk, Railway Tracks, Wishbone), which had violated gate 2.

story: A Bedsheet Cover is draped flat along the Horizon Line, and a Swaddling Wrap presses a wet inked page against it — peel it away and you hold a perfect COPY.
reading_story: Shaq clips a short 'sha', mashes the Swaddling Wrap under the Bedsheet Cover, and lifts a flawless COPY.

story: Inside a peaked Thatched House a Swaddle Basket rocks a baby, who reaches up and scrawls its very first written CHARACTER on the wall.
reading_story: Jee clips a sharp 'ji', peeks into the Thatched House, and reads the baby's first CHARACTER.

story: Atop a swaying Bamboo Grove, a lacquered Snap-Lid Bento clicks its lid down flush — that satisfying snap of a perfect fit is the ANSWER the quizmaster wanted.
reading_story: Tone Loc grabs the mic beneath the bamboo, and every time the crowd shouts a question he raps back the ANSWER without missing a beat.

story: A brave hero forces himself to STAND UP straight on top of the blazing round Sun, balancing on its scorching disc, and the hiss of his boots on the fire is the only SOUND for miles.
issues: Shares 立(stand up)+日(Sun) with 意(idea); the on-the-sun absurdity keeps them separable but watch for interference.

story: A deafening sound slams down like a press plate onto the soft heart below; with each thundering strike, the flattened heart squeezes out one fresh, fully formed IDEA.
reading_story: Mr. Eaton yells a clipped "ee!" each time his press stamps out another IDEA, selling them hot off the plate.

story: On the left, Puddle Splash flicks three fat droplets sideways; on the right a robed lord holds out an empty goblet, and the flung water streams straight into it as servants POUR.
reading_story: Chewbacca tips a barrel over the lord's cup, roaring a long "chuuuu" as gallons POUR out and drench everyone.
issues: Minor: reading_story implies the lord's cup is filled by Chewbacca's barrel, which loosely echoes the 主 'lord' component into the reading segment, but this is not etymological claim-making and stays within personas.

story: A Rake Hand claws a Bedsheet Cover off the bed on the left; on the right a Guillotine Blade drops beside a limp Hanging Towel — you snatch your towel and RETURN home for the night.
issues: Draft's components_used omitted 巾 (Hanging Towel); corrected to include it since the story already uses that actor. Four components make the scene slightly busy but all appear by exact name.

story: OLD: at a weathered Plus-Sign Crossroads, a wide Open Mouth sits sunk in the tarmac below, cracked and toothless, mumbling tales from ten generations ago.
issues: 'ten generations' is incidental flavor, not a competing component name; 十 is explicitly cast as Plus-Sign Crossroads, so no ambiguity.

story: Two Approval Stamps thunk down the left margin, each printing a bright red YES; on the right the Yawning Cavern drinks in every YES and belts them back as one soaring, echoing SONG.
reading_story: Carr the cabbie leans on his horn outside the theatre; the clipped "ka" swells until the whole marquee answers with a rousing SONG.
issues: Minor: main story says "Two Approval Stamps" but 可 appears only once in 歌; the doubling is a harmless embellishment, not a phantom component, so it passes gating but could be tightened to a single stamp for fidelity.

story: A wide Fishing Net is cast flat over the market stall, and dragged up in its mesh, dripping, sits one glossy Cowrie Shell — the coin you slap down to BUY.
reading_story: By snaps a Fishing Net over a fruit cart, scooping one Cowrie Shell into his fist — enough to BUY the whole cart.

story: A welded Scaffold Rack sags overhead, and through its missing-crossbar gap, cold rust drips onto the heart trapped below, staining it blacker and blacker — BAD.
reading_story: Acker gleefully salts the town well, cackling at the sputtering villagers — everything Acker touches turns BAD.

story: MAP: inside a square Walled Box with no gate, a long-handled Grain Dipper stands planted, its ladle-bowl scooping across the floor — charting every corner of the sealed enclosure.
reading_story: Zoo the keeper clips a short 'zu!' as he unrolls the MAP to find the trapped animal.
issues: Both supplied actors present; MAP leads. On-dominant (ず) so Zoo appears in reading_story; persona ('Zoo-keeper', short) matches. Clean two-component glyph, highly distinctive.

story: A Surveyor Wheel clicks off a field's full perimeter, then rides a Conveyor Belt gliding along the bottom-left road — one complete loop delivered marks off exactly one WEEK.
reading_story: A cobbler rolls a Shoe around a track once, each lap counting off a WEEK until seven scuffs mean the month is nearly done.
issues: Minor (non-gating): reading_story logic is loose — 'seven scuffs mean the month is nearly done' conflates weeks with a month (7 weeks is not ~a month); flavor only, does not affect the required Shoe actor presence.

story: The Thatched House lifts off the ground and lowers itself over the crater where the Landed Meteor lies steaming — peaked roof capping the rock completely, turning the crash site into a ROOM.
reading_story: Schitt inspects the crater ROOM and sniffs, "Shitsu! There's a meteor where the bed should be."

story: You wait beneath the bus stop's little roof; on the pavement below glitter a few coins — too few for any fare — so you shrug and WALK.
reading_story: Icy Hoth refuses the bus — he'd rather WALK, each short step puffing a clipped 'ho' of frost.

story: WIND howls through an open Goalpost Frame; a Falling Katana whips across the top, and inside the frame a Fat Grub clings for its life to the crossbar as the whole gusting kanji roars.
issues: '風' in components_used is the target kanji itself (already-learned self-reference); the three real actors (Falling Katana, Goalpost Frame, Fat Grub) all appear, so coverage holds.
'the whole gusting kanji roars' is mild filler but stays under the word cap.

story: A Spooled Thread on the left mashes its silk fibers into wet pulp; on the right a Family Crest Banner is pressed flat down onto it — peel them apart and you hold one smooth white sheet of PAPER.
reading_story: The Sheriff licks his thumb, tears a "shi"-crisp sheet of PAPER from his pad, and slaps down a WANTED poster on the saloon wall.
issues: Minor (non-gating): 糸 is glossed in-story as 'silk fibers' via the persona's silk-thread imagery, which is fine, but the phrase 'mashes its silk fibers into wet pulp' edges close to a plausible-sounding papermaking rationale; it reads as imaginative scene action rather than an etymology claim, so gate 6 still passes.
Minor (non-gating): main story is 39 words, right at the ~40 ceiling; no slack for future edits.

story: A Village Milestone sits up top, and below it a Coal Brazier's four glowing coals scorch the stone from underneath, smoke staining the whole marker sooty — that charred kanji is pure BLACK.
issues: '黒' in components_used is the target kanji itself (already-learned self-reference); the two real actors (Village Milestone, Coal Brazier) both appear.
'four glowing coals' faithfully matches the Coal Brazier registry image.

story: A Grass Tuft caps the top of a round-bottom Morphing Potion below it; the bubbling flask erupts mid-change, its liquid morphing into a single blazing FLOWER.
reading_story: Cabbie Carr clips his "ka" as he slams a FLOWER onto the dashboard, its petals fanning across the windshield of his cab.
issues: Minor (non-gating): 'below it' is mildly redundant after 'caps the top,' though it does reinforce the ⺾-over-化 vertical spatial relation.

story: SPRING festival: a Stepladder pokes up through three paper streamers strung overhead, its legs flaring wide, and tucked between its feet the Sun glows like a ground-lantern, warming the whole lane.
reading_story: Shunsuke the striker volleys the first ball of SPRING over the blossoming goalposts — petals burst off the net as it hits.

story: A Mound of Soil is heaped over glowing embers and fanned until the whole pile blushes a fierce, burning RED.
issues: Near-atomic glyph (kradfile leaves 赤 itself as a component); the ember-mound scene carries the keyword. Kun-dominant, no reading actor — correct.

story: Over a Mound of Soil capped by a Pot Lid and twin Railway Tracks, a Full Moon rises and washes the whole scene in cold, glowing BLUE.
issues: Over-decomposed (生 top split into 亠+二+土); all actors named and the moonlit-blue payoff lands. Kun-dominant, no reading actor — correct.

story: This grand BUILDING has a Heaped Rice Bowl steaming on the left counter, while on the right a Wax Seal Press stamps official red wax onto every guest's dinner reservation.
reading_story: Khan gallops through the marble BUILDING on horseback, hooves echoing, demanding to know which floor serves his feast.

story: Rain hisses off the Landed Meteor steaming in its crater — until the Draped Cloak flops down over it, sagging at the edges, becoming the meteor's first makeshift ROOF.
reading_story: Occam climbs onto the ROOF with his razor, shaving off every unnecessary shingle until one simple layer keeps out the rain.

story: A Swaddling Wrap folds down over a Coiled Cobra whose scales flash every shade of the rainbow — unwrap it and out spills pure COLOR.
issues: Kun-dominant, no reading actor — correct.

story: A sprinter kicks hard off a Mound of Soil at the starting block, legs already a blur — bursting into a flat-out RUN.
issues: Kun-dominant, no reading actor — correct.

story: A sprinter crouches to RUN, but the Coiled Garden Hose lashed to his back suddenly uncoils — nozzle-head snapping upright — and yanks him bolt-upright, wide-eyed. That jolt is how you WAKE UP.
reading_story: A locksmith's Key clicks in the dawn lock, and the whole house springs alive — lights, kettle, alarm — forcing every sleeper to WAKE UP.
issues: Minor: story is ~44 words (main story 42 words by my count), slightly over the ~40 word soft cap, but within tolerance given the '~' qualifier.

story: A golden Rice Stalk on the left leans into a crackling Bonfire on the right, ripe heads glowing like falling embers — harvest-time AUTUMN.
issues: Kun-dominant, no reading actor — correct.

story: Along a shimmering Horizon Line you jab a thumb at your own sweaty face (ONESELF) and drag one weary Trailing Footprint through the heat — the dead of SUMMER.
issues: Uses the learned kanji 自 (oneself) as an actor. Kun-dominant, no reading actor — correct.

story: A Feather Pair, laid side by side, sweeps down over a White Candle, snuffing then relighting its pale flame — sweep after patient sweep, the wings LEARN the exact motion.
reading_story: A Shoe drops onto the workbench, and the cobbler hammers the same rhythm over and over until his hands LEARN it by heart.

story: A Galloping Stallion skids to a halt beneath a Draped Cloak of iron awnings, snorting on the platform where every train pulls in — the STATION.
reading_story: Ecker clips 'eki', ties the Galloping Stallion under the Draped Cloak, and waits at the STATION.

story: A lone Woolly Ram stands chewing on a shrinking sandbar while, off to its left, a Puddle Splash flings three fat droplets that swell and swell until saltwater swallows the ram whole — the boundless OCEAN.
reading_story: Yoyo saws one long "yoooo" from his cello on the shore; the swelling note rolls outward and becomes the roaring OCEAN.
issues: Minor: story mentions 'saltwater' and 'shrinking sandbar' which are scene-dressing, not phantom components — acceptable, but keeps the actor count feeling slightly busy.
Minor: reading_story leans on 'yoooo' onomatopoeia to carry the long-vowel cue; it works but is the softest anchor in the card.

story: A Falling Katana slashes down at the left, and where it lands the whole compass of Direction spins wildly, needle whirling every way at once — pack your bags, you're off on a TRIP.
A red Wax Stamp presses down on the left; on the right a yellow Rubber Glove tugs a Full Moon down like a nightshirt over a shoulder — stamped, glove-smoothed, and moon-draped: your CLOTHING.
reading_story: Fokker the aviator zips into his fur-lined flight CLOTHING, clipping the buckle with a quick fuku before takeoff.
issues: Three actors make the main story slightly busy, but the dressing scene stays coherent.

story: The Crescent Moon, a single sharp orange sliver, tips sideways and pours molten dusk over the harbor, staining every sail amber — the first breath of EVENING.
reading_story: Sekka the chef flips one ladle skyward; it curves into a thin Crescent Moon and glazes the EVENING sky orange with a hiss of steam.
issues: Minor (non-gating): the registry reading_actor.note reads 'one ladle flip (seki)' / 'Ends in -ki coda', but reading is せき and actor_name is 'Sekka' — the note's 'seki'/'-ki coda' phrasing is internally muddled. The candidate correctly uses the supplied persona name 'Sekka', so actor consistency holds, but the registry note itself should be cleaned up.

Note (not a defect): dominant_reading is kun ゆう, yet the reading_story is built on the on'yomi actor せき/Sekka. This is legitimate per the supplied reading_actor and せき is a valid on'yomi of 夕, but a learner may find the ladle-flip 'seki' pun weakly tied to the everyday ゆう reading they'll actually meet in the vocab (夕方 ゆうがた, etc.).

story: A dealer flicks Crescent Moon cards across a felt table, each thin orange sliver landing on the last until the pile fans out huge and overflowing — so MANY you can't count them all.
reading_story: Tut deals Crescent Moon cards so fast his pile grows MANY times higher than yours.

story: DEATH: over the flat Horizon Line a Soup Ladle tips out cold broth, a Crescent Moon glints on the left, and beside it lies one Gnawed Rib-Bone picked clean in the dust.
reading_story: The clipped Sheriff nudges the Gnawed Rib-Bone with his boot, spits a sharp shi, and declares it plain DEATH.
issues: Follows the registry's four-actor decomposition (一+夕 also live inside 歹 visually, but all four are supplied components, so listing them is correct, not false etymology).

story: A straw Scarecrow at the left edge tips a Pot Lid over its head like a helmet, and beneath the brim a thin Crescent Moon glows — the field goes dark into deep NIGHT.
issues: Scarecrow is a thing, not a person; 'over its head' lightly anthropomorphises but stays within the registry image (a scarecrow does have a head), so acceptable.

story: A straw Scarecrow stretches its stick-arm up to the blazing Sun and begs to BORROW its warmth for just one cold afternoon.
issues: Kun-dominant, no reading actor — correct.

story: A Rake Hand drags the Sun across the sky while a Stumpy Sparrow hops one peg further along its perch — click, another DAY OF THE WEEK ticks past.
reading_story: Yoyo drawls a looong 'yoo', rakes the Sun past the Stumpy Sparrow, and names each DAY OF THE WEEK.
issues: Shares the reading actor Yoyo with 洋, but the rake-and-sparrow calendar scene is far from 洋's ocean, so interference is low.

story: A steaming Heaped Rice Bowl tips toward a Yawning Cavern of a mouth that gapes wide and gulps the broth down in one long DRINK.
issues: Kun-dominant, no reading actor — correct.

story: Inside the empty Goalpost Frame, a Stepladder unfolds — and draped over every rung, dripping and marbled, hang thick red steaks of raw MEAT curing in the open air.
reading_story: A Nicker knife slips from its sheath and carves one clean stripe down the slab of MEAT, splitting fat from muscle.

story: A SUBSTITUTE teacher, broke, pries a shining Cowrie Shell from the classroom trophy case and presses it into your palm: "Take it — just promise to LEND it back by Friday."
reading_story: Ty Cobb slides into a pawnshop, tosses his bat on the counter, and growls at the broker to LEND him a fistful of cash before the next game.
issues: Meaning placement is technically 'end' but the keyword LEND is trailed by 'it back by Friday' rather than being the absolute final word — the payoff punch is slightly softened. It still clearly lands as the pivotal verb of the closing line, so this passes Gate 4 but is the weakest gate.

The cowrie-shell-as-money image is shared across the 貝 (shell) kanji family, so the treasure/money motif alone could interfere with neighbors; the substitute-teacher + trophy-case theft framing is what carries the distinctiveness here.

story: Three Bean Sprouts poke up over a Bedsheet Cover; below, an Open Mouth sings out across a raised Mound of Soil, and the echo fills the great HALL.
reading_story: Doe drawls a looong 'doo', belts one note from the Open Mouth, and the sound floods the grand HALL.

story: A long-tailed Bird perches on a rail, and directly beneath it a row of glowing Coal Brazier embers roasts its dangling tail-feathers — one very startled, smoking BIRD.
issues: The 鳥 'component' is the whole target kanji (=bird), so it doubles as the keyword rather than a distinct sub-actor; acceptable since it is a supplied component.

story: On the left, a Heaped Rice Bowl steams under its lifted lid. On the right, an angry diner jams a Protest Placard skyward: "MORE FOOD NOW!" — the strike ends when they're served a full MEAL.
reading_story: Hancock sets down his quill mid-signature, grabs his chopsticks, and devours a steaming MEAL before adding one final flourish.

story: A Dodging Hare bolts left out of its snare and skids straight into a colossal Flexing Bicep on the right, which clamps down and hoists the terrified hare overhead like a barbell — sheer trembling EXERTION.
reading_story: Ben, sweat pouring, cranks the rusted lever with white-knuckled EXERTION until it groans and finally gives.

story: WINTER: the pond has frozen so hard that a Trailing Footprint sits pressed into its white surface, and trapped in the ice directly below, a single Ink Droplet hangs suspended mid-fall, jet-black against the frost.
reading_story: Tone the rapper performs on a frozen lake, stretching every bar looong, breath billowing white — his WINTER show freezes the mic to his glove.

story: A Folding Ruler snaps open into a sharp angle atop the Horizon Sunrise, clacking wider and wider to measure how high the sun climbs — the whole stretch it marks off is DAYTIME.
reading_story: Chewbacca sprawls across the Falcon's hull, shaggy fur blazing gold in the sun, roaring at anyone who wakes him before DAYTIME ends.

story: TEA: a wiry Grass Tuft sprouts on top, a leaning Stepladder shelters the leaves as they steep, and a sturdy Tree below props up the whole steaming teahouse.
reading_story: Chaplin twirls his cane with a clipped 'cha', tips his bowler, and sips a delicate cup of TEA beneath the tent.

story: A Falling Katana swishes down past Twin Pillars, where a taut Longbow leans and a Lightning Bolt cracks straight through the middle — the reckless little kid who grabbed all your weapons: your YOUNGER BROTHER.
issues: All four components (Falling Katana, Twin Pillars, Longbow, Lightning Bolt) present; keyword lands at end. Slightly busy with four small parts but coherent.

story: COW: one massive black-and-white heifer plants herself square in the barn doorway, horns tilted, tail flicking, chewing her cud and refusing to budge an inch.
issues: Single-component kanji; keyword leads. Smoothed 'single horn' to 'horns' to avoid an odd/false-feeling image detail (cows have two horns); actor and keyword unchanged.

story: On the left a cow strains against its rope, terrified of the tattered Skull-and-Crossbones Flag staked at its right flank — condemned livestock, no longer an animal to anyone, just a quarantined THING.
reading_story: A stick of Butter melts over the lost-and-found bin, gluing every THING inside into one greasy, unclaimable lump.

story: On the left a cow lowers her horns and rams the Bronze Temple Bell on the right; a deep BOOM floods the courtyard — she alone may ring it, because she is SPECIAL.
reading_story: Toker leans against the Bronze Temple Bell, takes one clipped puff, and blows a star-shaped smoke ring — his one SPECIAL trick.

story: A silver Fish flops onto a Rice-Paddy Grid, and beneath it a Coal Brazier glows with four hot coals, ready to grill your fresh-caught FISH to a crisp.
issues: All three components present (Fish, Rice-Paddy Grid, Coal Brazier); 'four coals' matches registry image. Keyword lands at end. Strong grill-the-fish scene.

story: A wide Open Mouth up top bellows orders down onto two stubby Wishing-Well Legs striding below — the bossy tall one who runs the household: your ELDER BROTHER.
issues: Both components present (Open Mouth, Wishing-Well Legs); kun dominant so no reading actor, correct. Keyword at end. Bossy-shouting persona differentiates well from 弟 (younger brother).

story: A big orange Starfish stands guard on the rock, and a single black Ink Droplet drips from one flung-out arm — the moment it lands, the whole starfish snarls, leashes itself, and becomes a bristling guard DOG.
reading_story: Ken the plastic doll clips a leash onto a snarling DOG; the doll's stiff arm jerks as the beast lunges, dragging Ken across the yard.
issues: Minor imageability wobble: 'the whole starfish snarls, leashes itself' is slightly abstract — a starfish self-leashing is hard to picture; the older 'ink droplet plops on like a wet nose' beat was more concrete for the 丶 dot. Not gating.

The 丶 Ink Droplet is present but its narrative role ('drips from one flung-out arm — the moment it lands') is now just a trigger rather than a distinct image tied to the dog (e.g. the nose), so it carries slightly less mnemonic weight than in the previous version. Still passes coverage.

story: On the left an Hourglass leans in; on the right dangles a hard, green Unripe Peach, its topmost twig still a sealed bud. Too little time, too little ripening — she is the YOUNGER SISTER.
reading_story: Mai reaches up but can't grasp the branch her big sister already picked clean — small, striving Mai, forever the YOUNGER SISTER.

story: On the left an Hourglass stands guard; on the right a striped Market Awning flaps on its tall pole. She rents the whole stall, hawks the produce, counts every coin — the bossy ELDER SISTER of the market.
reading_story: A Sheriff strolls the stalls, tips his hat with a clipped "shi!" — and even he pays full price to the ELDER SISTER running the awning.

story: A Puddle Splash flicks off the left bank; on the right a Grass Tuft crowns a Horizon Line laid over an Open Mouth, and beneath it an orange Starfish sprawls — a river-flooded field far off in CHINA.
reading_story: Khan reins his horse at the splashing river, mouth agape at the vast grassy fields of CHINA.
issues: Meaning story carries all five components; reading_story echoes river/mouth/grass so Khan ties cleanly to the same scene. Solid.
